scope: All six complete proposed Latin and reconstructed English bodies, including actual endings, embedded rubrics, the Queenship option, and communicative fidelity. Review performed independently from the root meaning assessments.
authority_boundary: This is a bounded review proposal, not an adoption, activation, publication-rights, or approved-liturgical-text decision. The root retains study-translation and admission authority. Changed body, source controller, or meaningful entry bytes need their own review; no vanished historical English receipt is treated as acceptance of these new bytes.
hash_convention: Body hashes are SHA-256 of exact UTF-8 text including terminal LF. File hashes cover exact file bytes. Object hashes use JSON UTF-8 with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True and separators=(comma, colon), without terminal LF.

target_image.locus: CMAA 1962 artifact p. 243, printed p. 162, no. 924; complete prayer and following response direction.

reasons: The opening retains God as addressee and Christ, our Lord, as the one whose Passion undoes the inherited death arising from the ancient sin. All succeeding generations correctly renders the collective posteritatis genus omne; nothing from the older main-text ending is imported.

Having been conformed to him refers to the same Christ and preserves the prayer's antecedent. The earthly-one/heavenly-one comparison, the necessity of nature, and sanctification by grace all remain. The inherited biblical allusion is preserved without inserting explanatory names into the prayer.

Through the same Christ our Lord accurately retains the entire printed Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum. conclusion. All respond: translates the printed direction and is typed nonspoken; Amen remains spoken.

The English is a complete, intelligible study rendering. The sanctification of grace is literal and somewhat abstract; the separate optional-wording file offers a nonblocking clarification, not a required correction.
cases.ending_check: Complete printed same-Christ ending retained; no further standard conclusion expansion.
cases.option_check: No internal optional wording in this bounded target.

reasons: The English resolves the Latin's opening ablative construction into now that the solemn rites ... have been celebrated and retains those rites as the subject of the petition. Its repetition of performed/celebrated reflects the source rather than omitting a clause.

The feast (commemoration) of Saint Mary our Queen retains the parenthetical memoria alternative and the complete identity. The rendering does not choose one alternative or merge both into a cumulative celebration.

Through her intercession ... bring us salvation preserves the intercessor and the benefit for us. Joyfully fulfilled in her honor retains the closing relative clause, its joy, and its Marian reference.
